claude says metal is infra failure:
```
The failure is an infrastructure/environment issue in the baremetalds-devscripts-setup step — the cluster never even got installed, so HAProxy/router code was never exercised. Specifically:

  1. Root cause: The Ansible task "Download Go tarball from official source" failed trying to download go1.24.10.linux-amd64.tar.gz from go.dev with an SSL error:
  Connection failure: [ASN1: NOT_ENOUGH_DATA] not enough data (_ssl.c:4192)
  2. This caused make requirements to fail with exit code 2, which meant the dev-scripts cluster provisioning never started — there's no kubeconfig, no cluster, and no test execution at all.
```

Another perf & scale run, and comparing to difference baselines:

- Against the [June 22 HAProxy 2.8 baseline](https://grafana.rdu2.scalelab.redhat.com:3000/d/d6105ff8-bc26-4d64-951e-56da771b703d/ingress-perf?orgId=1&from=now-6M&to=now&var-Datasource=beefdfd9-800e-430c-afef-383032aa2d1f&var-platform=AWS&var-clusterType=self-managed&var-infraNodesType=c5.4xlarge&var-ocpMajorVersion=5.0&var-termination=All&var-latency_metric=avg_lat_us&var-compare_by=uuid.keyword&var-all_uuids=All&var-uuid=7a03487f-ef49-4b7c-8795-da9bbd743add&var-uuid=0261bd18-2491-45f8-b312-558f6f6d5501&var-workerNodesCount=9), HAProxy 3.2 shows no regression for passthrough, a moderate 4-5% RPS drop for edge and HTTP terminations, and the most significant impact on reencrypt at 7% (HTTP/2) to 15% (HTTP/1.1).
- Against the [June 29 HAProxy 2.8 baseline](https://grafana.rdu2.scalelab.redhat.com:3000/d/d6105ff8-bc26-4d64-951e-56da771b703d/ingress-perf?orgId=1&from=now-7d&to=now&var-Datasource=beefdfd9-800e-430c-afef-383032aa2d1f&var-platform=AWS&var-clusterType=self-managed&var-infraNodesType=c5.4xlarge&var-ocpMajorVersion=5.0&var-termination=All&var-latency_metric=avg_lat_us&var-compare_by=uuid.keyword&var-all_uuids=All&var-uuid=7a03487f-ef49-4b7c-8795-da9bbd743add&var-uuid=39f0880f-9207-4172-8c02-2ae5bb9f78ac&var-workerNodesCount=9), HAProxy 3.2 shows no regression for passthrough, a moderate 3-4% RPS drop for edge and HTTP terminations, and a 6% (HTTP/2) to 12.5% (HTTP/1.1) drop for reencrypt.

Still showing up to 12-15% regression in encrypt. This is above our general threshold (~5%) for concern. Something we should probably look into. CC @rhamini3 @jcmoraisjr

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/router/pull/792):

>## Summary
>
>Update the default HAProxy version in the router container from 2.8 to 3.2 for OpenShift 5.0. This decouples the HAProxy 3.2 bump from the multi-version feature gate promotion, giving us earlier CI signal on HAProxy 3.2 without waiting for the IngressControllerMultipleHAProxyVersions feature to GA.
>
>## Impact
>
>**On-prem load balancer (MCO):** The `haproxy-router` image is used by the on-prem API load balancer. This bump changes the HAProxy version used there. If issues arise, the on-prem team can pin to the `haproxy-router-haproxy28` image instead.
>
>**MicroShift:** MicroShift manages its own router deployment using the `haproxy-router` image directly (already in the sidecar model). This bump updates their HAProxy version. If needed, they can switch to the `haproxy-router-haproxy28` image as a fallback.
>
>**OKD:** Requires a coordinating openshift/release PR (https://github.com/openshift/release/pull/82170) to bump the OKD router base image to the 5.0 stream, since the current stream lacks the `haproxy32` RPM (CentOS 10 dropped PCRE1 needed by haproxy28). These two PRs should be merged close together to minimize any gap in OKD CI.
>
>## Why now
>
>- Gets HAProxy 3.2 into the default CI payload immediately, rather than waiting for multi-version FG promotion (which may land close to pencils down)
>- Components still using the monolithic router image get bumped to 3.2, keeping them in sync with the default OCP HAProxy version
>- Any regressions from HAProxy 3.2 surface earlier in CI
>
>- **Brew build**: https://brewweb.engineering.redhat.com/brew/taskinfo?taskID=70996258
>- **Epic**: https://redhat.atlassian.net/browse/NE-2220
